crm_notes:
Summary: Verdance is a large telco exploring Redwood Dedicated for real-time conversational IVR and live-transcription at scale. Primary ask is a contractually guaranteed throughput profile (tokens/sec) across a reserved GPU pool plus predictable concurrency caps and an explicit burst policy. Procurement is pushing for hard SLOs and clear credit rules.

Key customer priorities (spoken on 2026-02-19 call):
- 'We need predictable behavior during traffic spikes — banking customers' IVR must not degrade.'
- Data residency and KMS integration (use on-prem HSM for keys).
- Clear fallback: when dedicated pool is saturated, route to private fallback model with documented latency & quality drop.

Throughput ask (initial):
- Minimum sustained throughput: 45,000 tokens/sec across the reserved pool (baseline guarantee).
- Concurrency cap (per route): 400 active conversational sessions (expected avg session throughput ~112 tokens/sec).
- Burst policy: allow spikes to 120,000 tokens/sec for up to 5 minutes using accumulated burst credits (token-bucket model). Bursts beyond that should trigger graceful degradation (shorter context, model fallback).
- Pre-warming: prefer pre-warm window of 10 minutes before large marketing events; Redwood to support scheduled pre-warm API.

Latency / SLO expectations:
- P95 generation latency target: <=120ms for typical requests (avg 256 tokens output).
- First-token latency (interactive): <80ms for routes on dedicated nodes.
- Availability target: 99.95% for dedicated pool; credit formula requested (days downtime -> pro-rated ARR credit).

Capacity planning notes:
- Preferred hardware: H100-style profile (customer willing to accept a mix of H100 + A100 equivalents if performance parity is documented).
- Expected peak pattern: daily peaks at 09:00-11:00 and 17:00-19:00 PST; occasional large campaign spikes once per quarter.
- Sequence length distribution: avg 256 tokens, p90 1024, max 4096 (for transcription bursts).

Commercial / legal asks:
- Want explicit SLA clause for minimum tokens/sec guarantee and automated scaling latency cap.
- Request for fallback pricing when routed to non-dedicated models (discounted token rate during fallback).
- Audit rights and quarterly security review slot.

Internal notes for Redwood AE/SE:
- SE Rajat to run a capacity-sizing workshop (3/10) with Verdance infra team to map pool size to guarantees.
- Deliver a revised SOW with concrete burst-credit accounting and credit schedule by 2026-03-08.
- Confirm KMS/HSM handshake flows with Security (ticket SEC-2109).

Quote/POC plan:
- 4-week PoC: reserved 6xH100-equivalent pool (sizing TBD in workshop), validated against 2 synthetic traffic patterns (steady and burst).
- Acceptance criteria: sustained >=45k tokens/sec for 30 minutes, bursts up to 120k tokens/sec with degraded fallback demonstrating <200ms p95 after fallback.

Customer sentiment: engaged but price-sensitive; procurement wants strong contractual protections. SE reports technical trust in Redwood runtime but needs clear measurement & credit math to present to finance.
